faces.f: Raksha watched as the goblins continued to pour onto the Razor Fields. "They just don't know when to stop, do they?"

"Her will shall banish the shadows. Her might shall punish the lawless. Her beauty shall restore the light."
—Ushanti, leonin seer
"Memnarch or the vedalken salvage most of the large machines, leaving us only scraps. Scraps are enough."
Each generation, a handful of Auriok girls are allowed to visit the Cave of Light. They return riding the wind and brandishing steel.
The cave floods with light. A thousand rays shine forth and meld into one.
"Memnarch shall rage against us. We shall endure."

"I may be kha, but without my soldiers, my people, I am nothing."
—Raksha Golden Cub
The loxodon ascribe religious superiority to those born albino, believing them to be spiritually pure.
Long ago, the Auriok attempted peace with the loxodons. The leonin attempted war. Neither succeeded.
Some believe that Raksha, youngest of the kha, is the reincarnation of Dakan, the first and mightiest of leonin leaders.
The Auriok learned perseverance from their forebears. They learned justice from the leonin.

"Yesterday's relics will determine the outcome of tomorrow's war."
—Ushanti, leonin seer

"If what I have seen comes to pass, we will need our guardians more than ever."
—Ushanti, leonin seer

"Like dawn's first light, blind the unprepared and banish the shadows."
—Skyhunter creed
Though the grip of a golem is strong, the grip of Auriok magic is far stronger.
Some blades seek their own wielders.

"All beings have an inner light. Let me show you yours."
—Ushanti, leonin seer
Sometimes "innovation" means "stealing another's secret before anyone else can."

"They are like their vedalken masters: untouchable, aloof, and omnipresent."
—Bruenna, Neurok leader
To look into its light is to meet the gaze of history.
Power begets power.
Vedalken weapons sold to outsiders are as dependable as the vedalken themselves.
Under its mists, the earth sleeps.
Æther portals drift across Mirrodin's surface, dragging creatures across time and space.
They only appear in emergencies, and emergencies never last long.

"Perhaps I should take Mirrodin apart and begin again."
—Memnarch

"I watched a ship sail right through it. I thought it was harmless . . . until I saw what it had done to the crew."
—Bruenna, Neurok leader
Even the clouds bend themselves to Memnarch's will, eager to swallow those who oppose him.
It is telling of the vedalkens' culture that they trust human couriers more than their own comrades.
The vedalken see other beings from a cold distance, as either experimental subjects or objects of study.
A vertical scream pierces the night air and echoes doom through the clouds.
It shuns everything except its next meal.
Its laughter drives needles through your mind.
Its precious corpses dance like puppets to attract mindless nim prey.

"Feel the burn of the mists. Master them. They will devour your enemies."
—Geth, keeper of the Vault
The necrogen may have taken its sight, but it can still taste the fear of its prey.
The deadliest killers serve only those who are not afraid to die.
Those who find death under the black sun's shadow cannot escape its pull.
Necrogen enflames certain emotional centers in the Morioks' brains: hate, aggression, and especially greed.
The Moriok scavenge for weapons, for armor, for food—and ultimately for their souls.
The Moriok call the black moon the Whisperer. At her apex, she whispers of power.
In the swirling mists, you could walk right up to one and not know until its teeth are in your throat.
Victims are lucky if they remember ever having had what was lost.
The Great Furnace's blessing is a spectacular sight, but the best view comes at a high cost.
For millennia they wandered from plane to plane, devouring all metal. Finally, their wanderings are over.
The path of least resistance is often through your enemies.
Baby dragons can't figure out humans—if they didn't want to be killed, why were they made of meat and treasure?
Perhaps he shuns technology. Perhaps he appreciates nature. Perhaps he doesn't know the difference.
There aren't *that* many ways to destroy a solid steel weapon, but somehow the goblins keep finding new ones.
When enough artifacts lie too long in the same place, their magical radiation weakens reality, opening rifts of unpredictable destructive power.
When you feel a rumble in the ground, hold perfectly still. One sound will bring the hellion.
"Well, I jammed the whatsit into the whackdoodle, but I think I broke the thingamajigger."
The Krark Clan believes it's caught an ogre. The ogre believes he's caught seven goblins.
Its open mouth is a furnace blast that blisters the skin. Its smoking fists are meteors that split the earth.
Among the Vulshok, the most prized blades are those that killed their original owners.
The Quicksilver Sea hissed and bubbled at the indignity. The Vulshok shaman just smiled.
On Mirrodin, mages who call upon the power of rust are shunned by their people and often turn mercenary to survive.
"Why learn hundreds of spells when you can learn only one and use it to steal hundreds?"
He's got an axe to grind.
Vulshok shamans summon spark elementals to burn paths through thick underbrush—or through goblin salvage squads.
Vulshok sorcerers train by leaping into electrified storm clouds. Dead or alive, they come back down with smiles on their faces.
A chorus of life heralds the arrival of Mirrodin's final sun.
To some the birth of the fifth sun was a sign of doom. To others it was a sign of salvation. But to all it was a sign.
Only Sylvok magic could truly capture the perfection of a Mirrodin sunrise.
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.

"Tracking a fangren pack is easy. Catching up to one is fatal."
—Viridian scout
A talented apprentice makes all things. The master makes all things possible.
The ouphes finally managed to still the clockwork monstrosity by catching themselves in its cogs.
Every scar is a lesson, every battle a test of what you have learned.
Any creature on a druid's shoulder is his family, any land under his feet his home.

"I have no fangs, yet I constantly bite. I have no scales, yet I slither through you. What am I?"
—Riddle of the viper's venom
"The Tangle loans you life. Spend it well."
It outnumbers you one to many.
A small band of elves pledged many years ago to avoid the Edges of Forgetting. They have remained hidden until now.
They know a hoverguard's only blind spot is directly above it.
These machines build fearsome visages out of scrap metal to scare off predators who would otherwise be eager to consume them.
It follows the green sun over Mirrodin's surface, spinning massive webs of whispersilk as it goes.
Souls and steel, the essence of Mirrodin. Memnarch lacks one but has an abundance of the other.
A dent marks every year of service, and it has as much rust as glory.
The energy that infuses the rings with life also melts them away, leaving only useless puddles of slag.
Those near the clock don't hear it anymore, but their every movement is in time with its ticking.
It binds the five suns in human form.
It is the moment of discovery, the triumph of the mind, the reimagining of past glory.
Amidst the darkest ashes grow the strongest seeds.

"All memory of your existence will be wiped from reality. You will die, and no one will mourn."
—Memnarch
The cube's surface is pockmarked with jagged runes that seem to shift when unobserved.
Its power source is time itself. It absorbs unused minutes and hours, bringing the end of existence always closer.

"It is all in my grasp. Every petty dream, every grand scheme, every soul, every fear. It all flows through me and from me."
—Memnarch
Outside, it reflects the suns' light. Inside, it harvests the suns' power.
Goblin cannon crews are known not for their aim but for their ability to dive for cover.
All the junk, refuse, and offal of the Krark Clan is diligently collected, melted down, and made into more junk, refuse, and offal.
Each eye sees a different possibility for tomorrow.
Each myr was designed to fill a specific role. This one, for example, was designed to stomp on other myr.
The Krark Clan enjoys pulling them apart just to watch them reassemble one another.
Hand-stitched, and marked by the blood of the Auriok.
Its transmissions are the word of Memnarch. It speaks, and metal bows.
Scholars say that arbiters exist on every world, created by an unknown hand to enforce justice.
Only a focused mind can survive it.
As the dawns break, the manta soars.
As the fifth sun joins the other four, new abilities awaken in the creatures of Mirrodin.

"We order them to stand, they stand. We order them to wait, they wait. We order them to die, they die."
—Pontifex, elder researcher
It takes off with a roar of superheated wind, startling wild pterons as they survey the ground below.
The model incorporated the fifth sun effortlessly, as if it had always known.
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.

"They don't move, do they?"
"Only for the wrong sort of people."
"Are *we* the wrong sort of people?"

Healing is a matter of time, but it is sometimes also a matter of opportunity.
—D'Avenant proverb

"When you have been bitten with fangs of granite, you start to long for the ivory sabers of tigers."
—Norin the Wary

"Cloak me in mystery, hide my names from my enemies, and let me draw from the well of power."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

"Keep your chain mail, warrior. I have my own form of protection."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

"When one's word is law, one's whim is equally binding."
—Calmont, Aysen bureaucrat
Benalia has a complex caste system that changes with the lunar year. No matter what the season, the only caste that cannot be attained by either heredity or money is that of the Hero.

"Out there, there are spirits, but here, there is wine."
—Blessing for the bounty of Kjeld

"Don't look at it! Maybe it'll go away!"
—Ib Halfheart, goblin tactician
"They're not your friends; they despise you. I'm the only one you can count on. Trust me."

"Hang out our banners on the outward walls; / The cry is still, 'They come'; our castle's strength / Will laugh a siege to scorn."
—William Shakespeare, *Macbeth*
Avenant's archers are also trained as poets, so that each arrow is guided by a fragment of verse.

"The dead may be beyond the law, but speaking the wisdom of the dead will afford no protection!"
—Calmont, Aysen bureaucrat
These tears of pain I weep to the skies, Not bitter drops, but water made divine. Each gem of sorrow slips, no longer mine, But proffered thus to echo other cries.
Glory surged through her and radiance surrounded her. All things were possible with the blessing of the Divine.

"All this nonsense made by mages
Rusts and crumbles through the ages."
—Aline Corralurn, "Inheritance"

"Sometimes even the smallest boon can save a life."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

"Someone once said that hipparions are to warriors what aesthir are to skyknights. Don't believe it."
—General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox

Even after the wall was breached in half a dozen places, the phalanxes fought on, standing solidly against the onrushing raiders. Disciplined and dedicated, they held their ranks to the end, even in the face of tremendous losses.

"In these, our final days, I offer this. Though we could not save Icatia, we gave our children time to grow, and love, before it fell."
—Ailis Connaut, diary
Icatia's once-peaceful towns faced increasing attacks from orcs and goblins as the climate cooled. By the time the empire fell, they were little more than armed camps.

"But who is to guard the guards themselves?"
—Juvenal, *Satires*

"Make people wait for what they want, and you have power over them. This is as true for merchants and militia as it is for cooks and couples."
—Gwendlyn Di Corci

Honorable in battle, generous in death.
—Motto of the Kjeldoran Royal Guard
The heartlink between soldier and steed is hatched with the aesthir struggling from its shell.

"The faith of Serra is borne on wings of hope."
—Gulsen, abbey matron

Before a woman marries in the village of Sursi, she must visit the land of the mesa pegasus. Legend has it that if the woman is pure of heart and her love is true, a mesa pegasus will appear, blessing her family with long life and good fortune.
A blazing light to drive out the shadows.
A shield of light admits no shadow.

"'Do you know, I always thought Unicorns were fabulous monsters, too? I never saw one alive before!' 'Well, now that we have seen each other,' said the Unicorn, 'if you'll believe in me, I'll believe in you.'"
—Lewis Carroll,
*Through the Looking-Glass*

"As the cavalry bore down, we faced them with swords drawn and pikes hidden in the grass at our feet. 'Don't lift your pikes 'til I give the word,' I said."
—Maeveen O'Donagh,
*Memoirs of a Soldier*

"For my confession they burned me with fire / And found that I was for endurance made."
—*The Arabian Nights*,
trans. Haddawy

"I too shall be brought low by death, but until then let me win glory."
—Homer, *Iliad, Book XVIII*

"Divine gifts are granted to those who are worthy."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest
Healers ultimately acquire the divine gifts of spiritual and physical wholeness. The most devout are also granted the ability to pass physical wholeness on to others.

One light, one blade, one purpose.
—Vow of the Serra Paladins

"You have almost completed your four years, my son. Soon you shall be a skyknight."
—Arna Kennerüd, skyknight
The strongest walls are made not of stone or steel but of the focused strength of warriors.

"I regret feeding Kaervek's hunger for power—far better to live with animals innocent of such ambitions."
—Jolrael

Not all victories require defeat.
—Onean idiom
I heard their eerie howling, the wolves calling their kindred across the frozen plains.

Just as the evil ones approached to slay Justina, she cast a great spell, imbuing her weapons with her own life force. Thus she fulfilled the prophecy: "In the death of your savior will you find salvation."
Out of the blackness and stench of the engulfing swamp emerged a shimmering figure. Only the splattered armor and ichor-stained sword hinted at the unfathomable evil the knight had just laid waste.
Thunder in the wind / no rain / peace mourns its passing.
These spirits of the air are winsome and wild and cannot be truly contained. Only marginally intelligent, they often substitute whimsy for strategy, delighting in mischief and mayhem.

Little dreamt could seem so cruel
As waiting for the wings outspread,
The jagged teeth, the burning eyes,
And dagger-claws that clench to nerves.

"What I want, I take."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage

"O! call back yesterday, bid time return."
—William Shakespeare,
*King Richard the Second*

"I reeled from the blow, and then suddenly, I knew exactly what to do. Within moments, victory was mine."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter,
Kjeldoran royal mage

"Catch good today. Start replacing crew tomorrow."
—Faysal al-Mousa, fisher captain, log

"Stray not onto the path of darkness, or be lost forever."
—Baki, wizard attendant

Up and down,
over and through,
back around—
the joke's on you.

"Nothing endures but change."
—Heraclitus

"Worlds turn in crucial moments of decision. Make your choice."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage

"A dash of cool water does wonders to clear a cluttered battlefield."
—Vibekke Ragnild, *Witches and War*

"Unknown spears / Suddenly hurtle before my dream-awakened eyes . . . ."
—William Butler Yeats, "The Valley of the Black Pig"

". . . [A]nd gives to airy nothing A local habitation and a name."
—William Shakespeare,
*A Midsummer-Night's Dream*

"As we neared, Belfar proclaimed the wall to be made of glass and went forward to prove it. We had no choice but to pull his hands free from where he had touched it, leaving flesh palmprints on the icy wall."
—Tross, Vainus Expedition leader
This spell, like many attributed to Drafna, was actually the work of his wife and former student, Hurkyl.

"Heed the lessons of our time: the forms of water may move the land itself and hold captive the fires within."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage

"I doubt any labyrinth minotaurs still live—but then we minotaurs are stubborn beings."
—Onatah, Anaba shaman

"Keep a green tree in your heart and perhaps the singing bird will come."
—Chinese proverb

"'We have no legs,' the warrior spat, 'for we have finished running.'"
—Vodalian folktale

"Oh, I had a conscience once. But alas, I seem to have forgotten where I put it."
—Chandler

Most human scholars believe that merfolk are the survivors of sunken Atlantis, humans adapted to the water. Merfolk, however, believe that humans sprang forth from merfolk who adapted themselves in order to explore their last frontier.
These beings embody the essence of true heroes long dead. Summoned from the dreamrealms, they rise to meet their enemies.

"While, like a ghastly rapid river,
Through the pale door,
A hideous throng rush out forever,
And laugh—but smile no more."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Haunted Palace"
Occasionally members of the Institute of Arcane Study acquire a taste for worldly pleasures. Seldom do they have trouble finding employment.
Relentless as the tides, souls dark as a moonless night. Bloodshed on their minds, and greed burning in their hearts like molten gold.
Nethya stiffened suddenly, head cocked as if straining to hear some distant sound, then fell lifeless to the ground.
Legend has it that serpents used to be bigger, but how could that be?

"It rose above our heads, above the ship, and still higher yet. No foggy, ice-laden sea in the world could frighten me more."
—General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox

"No one can catch what won't be caught."
—Kakra, sea troll

"Leviathan, too! Can you catch him with a fish-hook or run a line round his tongue?"
—*The Bible*, Job 41:1
She had expected death to roar, to thunder, to growl. She did not recognize it when it came hissing to her side.

"The Soul selects her own Society—
Then—shuts the Door—"
—Emily Dickinson,
"The Soul selects her own Society"

"Come one, come all! this rock shall fly From its firm base as soon as I."
—Sir Walter Scott, "The Lady of the Lake"

"Vodalian rank is displayed by the colors and patterns of their skin. Beware the color red; that is the badge of the empress's favor."
—Corbio, pearl diver

When no falcons fly, beware the sky.
—Femeref aphorism

" . . . [W]hen the trees bow down their heads, / The wind is passing by."
—Christina Rossetti,
"Who Has Seen the Wind?"
Although greatly prized among falconers, the zephyr falcon is capricious and not easily tamed.

"Mystic shadow, bending near me, / Who art thou? / Whence come ye?"
—Stephen Crane, "Mystic shadow, bending near me"

"Kings and beggars, they end the same—
Surrounded by stench, rot, and blame."
—Aline Corralurn, "Legacy"
Battle doesn't need a purpose; the battle is its own purpose. You don't ask why a plague spreads or a field burns. Don't ask why I fight.
On guard for larger dangers, we underestimated the power and speed of the imp's muck-crusted claws.
Their stench was vile and strong enough, but not nearly as powerful as their hunger.
'Twas in the bogs of Cannelbrae My mate did meet an early grave; 'Twas nothing left for us to save In the peat-filled bogs of Cannelbrae.
The thrulls bred at a terrifying pace. In the end, they overwhelmed the Order of the Ebon Hand.
"War is no picnic," my father liked to say. But the ants seemed to disagree.

"Every forest is carpeted with the corpses of a thousand trees."
—Baron Sengir to Autumn Willow

"The derelor's greatest contribution to the Ebon Hand was the inspirational effect its creator's execution had upon the other thrull breeders."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. II*

"The dead make good soldiers. They can't disobey orders, they never surrender, and they don't stop fighting when a random body part falls off."
—Nevinyrral,
*Necromancer's Handbook*
The highway of fear is the shortest route to defeat.

"Angels are simply extensions of truth upon the fabric of life—and there is far more dark than light."
—Baron Sengir

"There are some qualities, some incorporate things, / That have a double life, which thus is made / A type of twin entity which springs / From matter and light, evinced in solid and shade."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "Silence"

"Turn the key deftly in the oiled wards,
And seal the hushed casket of my soul."
—John Keats, "To Sleep"

"Two legs by day, four legs by night, eyes raging in storm-gotten might."
—Ancient Northland riddle

"We are no longer Nature's children, but her masters . . . ."
—Oath of the Ebon Hand

"They shall drink sorrow's dregs. They shall kill those whom once they loved."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer

"Kjeldorans should rule supreme, and to the rest, death!"
—Avram Garrisson, Leader of the Knights of Stromgald
Some Krovikans find strength in the ears and eyes of their victims and wear such fetishes into battle.

"Bind me to thee, my soul to thine. I am your servant and your slave. Blood for blood, flesh for flesh, Leshrac, my lord."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer
Her hand gently beckons, she whispers your name—but those who go with her are never the same.
An end to reason, an end to order. Forget all that has been.
The hardest of wizards can have the softest of minds.
When Raganorn unsealed the catacombs, he found more than the dead and their treasures.
Necrites killed Jherana Rure, ending the counterinsurgency.
The nightmare arises from its lair in the swamps. As the poisoned land spreads, so does the nightmare's rage and terrifying strength.
Sometimes the smallest nuisance can be the greatest pain.

"Should you a Rat to madness tease Why ev'n a Rat may plague you . . . ."
—Samuel Coleridge, "Recantation"
"Aw, he's just a silly, dirty little man. What's to be afraid of?"

"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose,
Nor spake, nor moved their eyes;
It had been strange, even in a dream,
To have seen those dead men rise."
—Samuel Coleridge,
"The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"

"Evil is relative. Do sheep think any better of the shepherd?"
—Baron Sengir

"We have always counted time with sand; this pinch is your meaningless life."
—Nailah, self-proclaimed Queen of Rabiah
When the alliance between Balduvia and Kjeldor deprived Stromgald of easy victories, its agents were forced to fuel their rituals with their own flesh.

Once I had the strength but no wisdom; now I have the wisdom but no strength.
—Persian proverb

"Until the Rebellion, thrulls served their masters faithfully—even at the cost of their own lives."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. II*

"It helps pass the time until you die."
—Grandmother Sengir

"What was yours is mine. Your land, your people, and now your life."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer

"For something is amiss or out of place / When mice with wings can wear a human face."
—Theodore Roethke, "The Bat"

"Good neighbors make good walls."
—Jakkarak the Maimer
He controlled the zombies even before his own death; now nothing can make them betray him.

"Fair fight? I'll take survival over chivalry any day!"
—Tor Wauki, Bandit King
The bane of all artificers, the legendary atogs devoured intricate tools to further their own twisted growth.

"Four things that never meet do here unite
To shed my blood and to ravage my heart,
A radiant brow and tresses that beguile
And rosy cheeks and a glittering smile."
—*The Arabian Nights*, trans. Haddawy

"Modern Sarpadia's swarming with thrulls. It's a testament to the orcs that they've survived there so long."
—Elbieta, Argivian scholar
Fire is never a gentle master.

"Every field watered in warriors' blood is sacred ground. Lay it not to waste, but claim it for our own—for glory, and for Stromgald!"
—Avram Garrisson, Leader of the Knights of Stromgald
Manticores divide all beings into two categories: other manticores and dinner.

"Often greatly outnumbered in battle, dwarves relied on catapults as one means of damaging a large army."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*

"Orc must die / Orc must die / Not an orc? / March on by."
—Dwarven marching song

"There is no shame in solitude. The lone knight may succeed where a hundred founder."
—Arna Kennerüd, skyknight
Warriors of the Tsunami-nito School spend years in training to master the way of effortless effort.
Brimstone marks this drake's territory. Unfortunately for travelers, all of the Burning Isles smell likewise.

"And topples round the dreary west A looming bastion fringed with fire."
—Alfred, Lord Tennyson, "In Memoriam"

"The spirit of the flame is the spirit of change."
—Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain
The secret of destruction is simple: everything burns.

"O! it is excellent / To have a giant's strength, but it is tyrannous / To use it like a giant."
—William Shakespeare,
*Measure for Measure*

"From down here we can make the whole wall collapse!"
"Uh, yeah, boss, but how do we get out?"

"When you're a goblin, you don't have to step forward to be a hero—everyone else just has to step back!"
—Biggum Flodrot, goblin veteran
To be king, Numsgil did in Blog, who did in Unkful, who did in Viddle, who did in Loll, who did in Alrok . . . .

"Goblins charge with a deafening war cry. The cry doesn't mean anything—it just drowns out the drums!"
—Reod Dai, mercenary

"Goblins bred underground, their numbers hidden from the enemy until it was too late."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*
Fortunately, hill giants have large blind spots in which a human can easily hide. Unfortunately, these blind spots are beneath the bottoms of their feet.

The minotaurs of the Hurloon Mountains are known for their love of battle. They are also known for their hymns to the dead, sung for friend and foe alike. These hymns can last for days, filling the mountain valleys with their low, haunting sounds.
With the horrible mask, Lagfrak the Low terrorized the countryside. But then he met Il-Chunt, the mask's model . . . .

"Yes, I think 'toast' is an appropriate description."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

"Some have said there is no subtlety to destruction. You know what? They're dead."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

"Some have said there is no subtlety to destruction. You know what? They're dead."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage
Generations of genetic weeding have given rise to the deviously cowardly Ironclaw clan.

"The raging waters had swept away trees, bridges, and even houses. My healers had much work to do."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest
What if they threw a war, and *everybody* came?

The intricate dynamics of Rundvelt goblin affairs are often confused with anarchy. The chaos, however, is the chaos of a thundercloud, and direction will sporadically and violently appear. Pashalik Mons and his raiders are the thunderhead that leads in the storm.

"Folklore has it that to capture a mountain goat is a sign of divine blessing. I just know it's a sign that dinner is on the way."
—Klazina Jansdotter, Leader of the Order of the Sacred Torch
In a rare display of ingenuity, the orcs invented an incredibly destructive weapon. Most orcish artillerists are those who dared criticize its effectiveness.
There's a chance to win every battle.
There is no natural disaster quite like orcish farming.
It's bigger than it thinks.

"Just the thing for those pesky water mages."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

"Hi! ni! ya! Behold the man of flint, that's me! / Four lightnings zigzag from me, strike and return."
—Navajo war chant

"I fear anything with teeth measured in handspans!"
—Norin the Wary
Chains of leaping fire and sizzling lightning laid waste the artificers' handiwork, sparing not a single device.

While it's true most dragons are cruel, the Shivan dragon seems to take particular glee in the misery of others, often tormenting its victims much like a cat plays with a mouse before delivering the final blow.

While it's true most dragons are cruel, the Shivan dragon seems to take particular glee in the misery of others, often tormenting its victims much like a cat plays with a mouse before delivering the final blow.

"The spirit of the stone is the spirit of strength."
—Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain
After years of being bullied, Fergo reaped the benefits of his newfound strength: he never met a man he didn't want to fight.

"Struggle, and you will only fan the flames."
—Talibah, embermage

The ground itself lends its strength to these walls of living stone, which possess the stability of ancient mountains. These mighty bulwarks thwart ground-based troops, providing welcome relief for weary warriors who defend the land.

"'Tis the set of sails, and not the gales,
Which tells us the way to go."
—Ella Wheeler Wilcox, "Winds of Fate"

"Walls? What walls?"
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

"Joskun and the other constables serve with passion, if not with grace."
—Devin, faerie noble
One auroch may feed a village, but a herd will flatten it.
